mainEntity.name: How much does a BMW 5 Series 524td engine replacement cost in the UK?

acceptedAnswer.text: A rebuilt M21D24 engine for a BMW 524td typically costs £3,000-£4,500 supply-only, with used units from £800 and reconditioned from £1,800. Fitting adds approximately 10-14 hours of labour at specialist rates.

mainEntity.name: What are the signs of timing belt failure in a BMW 524td?

acceptedAnswer.text: The M21D24 uses a timing belt, not a chain. Warning signs include a ticking noise from the front of the engine, difficulty starting, or visible cracking on the belt itself during inspection. BMW recommends replacement every 40,000km (approx. 25,000 miles).

mainEntity.name: Is it worth replacing the engine in a BMW 524td?

acceptedAnswer.text: The 524td is BMW's first production diesel and has genuine classic status. An E28 524td in good condition is worth £2,000-£6,000; an E34 524td £3,000-£8,000. If your car is solid and the replacement cost makes financial sense, many owners choose to invest.

mainEntity.name: How long does a BMW 524td engine replacement take?

acceptedAnswer.text: A typical BMW 524td engine replacement takes 2-3 days for a specialist workshop, including removal, fitting, and testing. Supply-only delivery is usually 1-3 working days. Complexities like turbocharger re-fitting or EDC system setup may add time.

mainEntity.name: What's the difference between the E28 and E34 BMW 524td engines?

acceptedAnswer.text: Both generations use the same M21D24 2.4-litre turbo-diesel with 115hp. The E34 version received a smaller turbocharger for improved responsiveness and Bosch EDC electronic diesel control, plus an oxidation catalytic converter from 1989.

mainEntity.name: What warranty comes with a BMW 524td replacement engine?

acceptedAnswer.text: Every rebuilt or reconditioned BMW 524td engine supplied through EnginesMarket carries a minimum 12-month unlimited-mileage warranty. Some suppliers offer extended coverage on premium rebuilds. Always confirm exact terms with your chosen supplier.

historyTimeline.h2: BMW 5 Series 524td - Engine History & Specs at a Glance
historyTimeline.intro: The BMW 524td made history in 1983 as BMW's first-ever production diesel car, proving that diesel power could be smooth, refined and genuinely enjoyable to drive. The M21 turbo-diesel engine powered two generations of 5 Series, the E28 (1982-1987) and E34 (1987-1991), before being replaced by the more advanced M51 diesel family.

milestones.description: **1982** - E28 524td launched with M21D24 2.4-litre turbo-diesel, 115hp, 210Nm torque, Garrett T3 turbocharger
**1987** - E34 524td introduced, carrying over the M21D24 engine but with a smaller turbocharger for improved responsiveness and Bosch EDC electronic diesel control - a world first
**1989** - Oxidation catalytic converter fitted as standard to improve emissions compliance
**1991** - 524td replaced by 525tds with the new M51 2.5-litre diesel engine

historyTimeline.closingNote: Every engine fitted to the BMW 5 Series 524td is covered below, with UK rebuilt pricing and known failure points.

commonProblems.h2: BMW 5 Series 524td Engine Problems - Repair Cost vs Replacement
commonProblems.h3: The BMW 524td's M21D24 is a generally robust engine, but age and mileage bring specific challenges. Timing belt failure and cooling system neglect are the two biggest threats to the 524td's 2.4-litre turbo-diesel. Rebuilt M21D24 engines through EnginesMarket include upgraded components addressing these failure points, plus a minimum 12-month unlimited-mileage warranty.

problems.h4: Timing Belt Failure - Why the BMW 5 Series 524td M21D24 Needs Regular Belt Changes
problems.rootCause: The M21D24 is an interference engine - if the timing belt breaks, pistons collide with valves, causing catastrophic internal damage. Belts degrade with age as well as mileage, making regular replacement essential.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: New timing belt, tensioner, and water pump (while accessible)
repairOptions.longevity: Essential maintenance every 25k-40k miles - the cheapest option by far
When belt has failed or head is cracked/warped

problems.vehicleValueCheck: A typical E28 524td (1982-1987) in average condition is worth roughly £2,000-£6,000; the E34 524td (1987-1991) typically sits in the £3,000-£8,000 bracket [THIRD-PARTY]. If you're facing a full rebuilt engine at £3,000-£4,500 plus fitting, the replacement cost may approach or exceed 60% of a lower-value E28's market value. For E34 examples and well-maintained E28s, the maths is more favourable.
problems.recommendation: If your 524td's timing belt is overdue - and you don't know when it was last changed - replace it immediately. This is the single most cost-effective preventative measure you can take. If the belt has already failed or the aluminium head has cracked from overheating, a rebuilt M21D24 with warranty is the sensible route. Given the 524td's growing classic status, many owners choose to invest in a quality rebuild rather than scrap a historic BMW.

problems.h4: Overheating & Cylinder Head Cracking - Cooling System Neglect in the 524td
problems.rootCause: The M21D24's aluminium cylinder head is vulnerable to warping and cracking if the cooling system isn't maintained. Water pump belt failure can cause rapid overheating.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Water pump, thermostat, coolant flush, belt replacement
repairOptions.longevity: Preventative - recommended every 5 years or 60k miles

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Head removal, skim/test, new gasket, pressure test
repairOptions.longevity: Only if damage is minor and the block is sound
When head is beyond repair or block damage has occurred

problems.vehicleValueCheck: Same as above - E28 524td values typically £2,000-£6,000; E34 524td values £3,000-£8,000. Cylinder head repair at £1,200-£2,500 is often a viable option, but if the head is cracked beyond repair, the replacement maths changes.
problems.recommendation: Preventative cooling system maintenance is cheap relative to the alternatives. Replace the water pump and belt proactively, and keep the cooling system in good order. If your 524td has overheated, get the head inspected promptly - catching a minor warp early can save the engine. For a car with classic status, a quality rebuild often makes more sense than repeated patch-up repairs.
